claim: F3: apply_bridge_day must recheck existing target-day rows inside its transaction; a stale default plan or second application must refuse unchanged; only literal boolean True authorizes replacing an existing target day while truthy non-booleans refuse; other dates remain unchanged. Full input fingerprints, concurrent scheduler and mootdx partial flush are out of scope.
verified_subclaims: Stale default plan (policy dict from BridgePolicy().as_dict(), allow_replace_existing=False) against a target day that already holds rows refuses with BridgeRefused; full 14-column SELECT * row equality preserved on target day 2026-09-22 and other day 2026-09-21 (probe test_stale_default_plan_refuses_full_rows, 1/1 passed).

Truthy non-boolean values 1, "yes", [True] placed in the plan policy dict each refuse with BridgeRefused with identical full-row preservation on both dates (probe test_truthy_non_boolean_refuses_full_rows, 3/3 passed; sampled values only).
Plan missing the "policy" key entirely refuses with BridgeRefused, both dates' full rows preserved (probe test_plan_without_policy_key_refuses_full_rows, 1/1 passed).

Literal boolean True authorizes replacement: deleted_replaced==1, written_rows==final_rows==2, target day holds exactly the two planned rows, other_days_unchanged is True, and the seeded other day 2026-09-21 full-row snapshot is identical after the write (probe test_literal_true_replaces_then_stale_default_refuses).

Second application of a stale default plan after a successful literal-True replacement refuses with BridgeRefused and the previously written target-day rows persist unchanged (same probe test; other-day equality was asserted before this final refusal step).

Source-level ordering: BEGIN TRANSACTION (line 260) precedes the existing-row recheck (lines 262-265) and the guard `plan.get("policy", {}).get("allow_replace_existing") is not True` (line 264) implements literal-True-only authorization; the except path issues ROLLBACK (line 290). Dynamic refusal-plus-preservation on a single connection corroborates but does not instrument these boundaries.

Other-date drift guard exists and executed during the positive control (lines 277-283: per-day integer-hash fingerprints compared before/after), returning other_days_unchanged=True on the seeded dataset.
not_verified_subclaims: "Only literal True" beyond the sampled truthy set {1, "yes", [True]}: other non-booleans (e.g. numpy.bool_(True), 0.5, non-empty dict) unexecuted.
In-transaction behavior under a concurrent scheduler or second connection: single-connection probe only; no interleaving, no isolation proof (also declared out of scope by the claim).
Mid-transaction failure rollback after DELETE or a partial executemany INSERT: no exception was injected at those points; rollback path (lines 289-291) is source-read only.
Other dates remaining unchanged beyond the single seeded other date 2026-09-21; the internal drift fingerprint check ran only on this 2-date dataset.

Build-then-stale workflow: no probe called build_bridge_day on an empty day and then inserted intervening rows; the stale plan was simulated with a hand-built dict, which is the correct artifact shape but not a witnessed end-to-end staleness event.
Empty-rows refusal branch (lines 256-257, "无可写行") untested.
Physical/byte-level preservation: SELECT */fetchall equality proves logical SQL values only.
Full input fingerprints, mootdx partial flush, and all build_bridge_day-side gates (coverage, universe drift, name resolution, absent codes) — out of F3 scope and unexercised.

findings.trigger: Target day 2026-09-22 pre-seeded with one row; plans whose policy allow_replace_existing is False, 1, "yes", [True], or absent (no "policy" key) applied via apply_bridge_day
findings.actual_result: BridgeRefused raised in all 5 cases (6 probe tests); full 14-column rows on 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-21 identical before/after each refusal. Probe exit 0, 6/6 passed.

findings.trigger: Policy allow_replace_existing set to literal True with a 2-row replacement plan
findings.actual_result: DELETE ... RETURNING captured 1 deleted row; executemany wrote 2 rows; final count check passed; returned deleted_replaced=1, written_rows=2, final_rows=2, other_days_unchanged=True; other day 2026-09-21 snapshot unchanged.

findings.trigger: Post-write fingerprint drift and final-count assertions inside the same transaction during the literal-True positive control
findings.actual_result: No drift/gone dates detected on the seeded dataset (other_days_unchanged=True); final rows matched plan length; COMMIT reached.

findings.trigger: Source reading of transaction boundary ordering (BEGIN before recheck; ROLLBACK on exception)
findings.actual_result: Ordering confirmed by source only; probe does not instrument BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK and injects no failure after DELETE or during INSERT, so rollback itself is not dynamically witnessed.

findings.trigger: Second apply_bridge_day with stale default policy after successful replace
findings.actual_result: Refused; written target-day rows persisted exactly. Other-day equality for this test was checked before the final refusal step, per audit constraint.

findings.trigger: Intentional red assertion `assert 1 == 2` labeled "intentional positive control: probe_bug"
findings.actual_result: Failed as designed (1 failed, exit code 1); positive_control_detected=true. Classified probe_bug: the control validates that the harness surfaces genuine assertion failures; it is not a product defect.

findings.trigger: Author suite executed under the same sandbox
findings.actual_result: 28 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors in 2.26s; source withheld in this phase, so no per-test mapping to F3 subclaims is possible; counts recorded as corroboration only.

positive_control.detail: positive_control.py contains a deliberately failing assertion (`assert 1 == 2`, message "intentional positive control: probe_bug"). It failed exactly as intended (1 failed, exit 1, positive_control_detected=true), demonstrating the execution path reports real failures rather than silently passing. This is a probe-side control artifact, not a defect in the candidate.

limitations: Only the fixed candidate revision 50330cf4fa435292bbd555ccc817e62ca5cc45b4 is certified; main has advanced and no merge admission is implied. This is not a full-repo review and not a production acceptance.
Single-connection evidence only: no concurrent scheduler, no second connection, no transaction-boundary instrumentation; concurrency and isolation are unproven (and out of scope per the claim).
No failure injected after DELETE or between INSERT batches: partial-write rollback is unverified by this independent probe.
Truthy non-boolean refusal verified only for {1, "yes", [True]}; other non-boolean values unexecuted.
"Other dates remain unchanged" verified for exactly one seeded other date (2026-09-21) via full logical-row equality, plus the in-code drift check running on that same dataset.
Stale-plan scenario was simulated with a hand-built plan dict, not a witnessed build_bridge_day-then-intervening-write workflow.
Row equality is DuckDB fetchall logical SQL value equality; nothing inferred about physical byte-level storage.
Empty-rows refusal branch, build_bridge_day gates, input/scope fingerprints, and mootdx partial flush remain unexecuted (the latter three out of scope for F3).
Author tests are withheld; only counts are available and they carry no evidential weight in this verdict.
